document: Every marathon edition the edition policy of this release leaves out of pooled statistics: category, reason, whether a record of it keeps an own-record view, and its raw, deduplicated and timing-eligible records. Rows are arrays in the order of `columns`; `reason` is an index into `reasons`. Outputs of the release state `policy_sha256`, `editions_sha256` and `counts` and are checked against this file.

Only about 500 of the roughly 6,000 finishers were loaded, from individual result pages, and 24 runners appear two or three times under name variants; the records are neither the full field nor a sample of it.

Our audit, not the producer, flags this edition: its checkpoints mix two timing bases (the 5 km reading came from separate runner pages). 1,877 of 4,463 complete grids put the finish at or before 40 km, and the rows that pass the timing checks still run 5–10 km up to about 30% slower than 10–15 km.
Producer explicitly force-dropped this incomplete 5 km grid.
Source notes identify top-500 result PDFs, not a representative full marathon field; the 770 records are all men.

The 25–40 km checkpoints are missing for about a third of finishers, and 40% of the complete grids have an impossible last section (checkpoint times include the start delay, the finish does not). The 40% of finishers that pass the timing checks are not a sample of the field.

The 35 km mat stopped recording partway through the field: 35 km is missing for 2,729 of 8,665 finishers, almost all of them slower ones, so complete timings survive for 95% of the quarter with the shortest finish times but 1% of the quarter with the longest.

The 40 km mat stopped recording late in the race: 40 km is missing for 267 of 1,809 finishers, almost all of them slower ones, so complete timings survive for nearly all of the three quarters with the shortest finish times but 41% of the quarter with the longest.

The 40 km mat stopped recording partway through the field: 40 km is missing for 685 of 1,654 finishers, so complete timings survive for 97% of the quarter with the shortest finish times and none of the quarter with the longest.

The checkpoint times include the start delay but the finish does not: half of the complete grids have an impossible last section, and the finishers that pass the timing checks are mostly the faster, earlier starters (80% of the quarter with the shortest finish times, 18% of the quarter with the longest).

The producer flags the 25 km mat as sitting about 0.6 km early, so every finisher’s 20–25 km section is short and 25–30 km long; the checkpoint timings do not measure the sections they are labelled with.

The producer flags the 30 km mat as sitting about 0.4 km late, so every finisher’s 25–30 km section is long and 30–35 km short; the checkpoint timings do not measure the sections they are labelled with.

The race was cut short in the heat: the course closed after about 3.5 hours and runners still on it were re-routed. The producer flags 1,734 recorded finishes, missing their 30–40 km checkpoints, as finishes on a shortened course, and no recorded finish is slower than 7:13 (8:15 or later in every other Chicago year). A finisher set cut off when a race was stopped is not comparable with other editions.

The race was stopped after the bombings near the finish, so the recorded finishers are only those who finished before the course closed (none slower than 4:45). A finisher set cut off by finish time is not comparable with other editions.

The source list for this edition mixes in 10 km-type finishes and unfinished runs whose last checkpoint was stored as the finish. The rows that can be identified are removed, and the producer says others may remain, so the edition supplies no pooled statistic.
